items.question: Under what conditions has in-ground-effect (IGE) hover controllability been substantiated for the R44 II?
options: 10 knot headwind up to 8000 feet density altitude
17 knot wind from any direction up to 9800 feet density altitude
Calm wind only at sea level
25 knot tailwind up to 5000 feet density altitude
items.explanation: The GENERAL paragraph of Section 5 states that IGE hover controllability has been substantiated in a 17 knot wind from any direction up to 9800 feet (2990 m) density altitude.

items.question: To what density altitude has IGE hover controllability been substantiated, as stated in the Performance section?
items.explanation: Section 5 states that IGE hover controllability has been substantiated up to 9800 feet (2990 m) density altitude.

items.question: What caution is given about the performance data presented in Section 5?
options: Data were obtained under typical operational conditions and may be pessimistic
Data were obtained under ideal conditions and actual performance may be substantially less
Data include a built-in safety margin that guarantees actual performance will be better than shown
Data apply only to new helicopters and not to in-service aircraft
items.explanation: The CAUTION in Section 5 explains that the performance data were obtained under ideal conditions and that performance under other conditions may be substantially less.

items.question: What assumption about indicated airspeed is made for the performance charts in the R44 II POH?
options: They assume a constant 5 knot instrument error
They assume a 3% high instrument error
They assume calibration only at 100 KIAS
items.explanation: Section 5 states that indicated airspeed shown on charts assumes zero instrument error.

items.question: To what outside air temperature at sea level has satisfactory engine cooling been demonstrated for the R44 II?
items.explanation: The DEMONSTRATED OPERATING TEMPERATURE paragraph states that satisfactory engine cooling has been demonstrated to an outside air temperature of 38 C (100 F) at sea level.
references: R44 II POH Sec 5: DEMONSTRATED OPERATING TEMPERATURE (p.5-1)

items.question: At altitude, satisfactory engine cooling has been demonstrated to what temperature margin above ISA?
items.explanation: Section 5 states that satisfactory engine cooling has been demonstrated to 23 C (41 F) above ISA at altitude.
references: R44 II POH Sec 5: DEMONSTRATED OPERATING TEMPERATURE (p.5-1)

items.question: In the IGE hover ceiling chart, what skid height is assumed for in-ground-effect hover?
items.explanation: The IGE HOVER CEILING VS GROSS WEIGHT chart specifies in-ground-effect hover at a 2 foot skid height.
references: R44 II POH Sec 5: IGE HOVER CEILING (p.5-3)

items.question: Which power and wind conditions are assumed in the IGE hover ceiling chart?
items.explanation: The IGE hover ceiling chart is labeled FULL THROTTLE, ZERO WIND.
references: R44 II POH Sec 5: IGE HOVER CEILING (p.5-3)

items.question: In the out-of-ground-effect (OGE) hover ceiling chart, which power condition is specified?
items.explanation: The OUT OF GROUND EFFECT hover ceiling chart is labeled TAKEOFF POWER OR FULL THROTTLE.
references: R44 II POH Sec 5: OGE HOVER CEILING (p.5-4)

items.question: According to the Height-Velocity diagram in the Performance section, what general guidance is given regarding the shaded areas?
options: Use shaded areas for best performance
Operate only in shaded areas during training
Stay below the shaded areas at all times
items.explanation: The HEIGHT-VELOCITY DIAGRAM for the R44 II is annotated with the instruction AVOID OPERATION IN SHADED AREAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 5: HEIGHT-VELOCITY DIAGRAM (p.5-5)

items.question: According to the PERFORMANCE DEFINITIONS in Section 1, how is calibrated airspeed (KCAS) defined?
options: Indicated airspeed corrected for instrument and position error
True airspeed corrected for altitude and temperature
Indicated airspeed corrected for temperature only
Groundspeed corrected for wind and slope
items.explanation: In the PERFORMANCE DEFINITIONS of Section 1, calibrated airspeed (KCAS) is defined as indicated airspeed corrected for instrument and position error.
references: R44 II POH Sec 1: PERFORMANCE DEFINITIONS (p.1-6)

items.question: According to the PERFORMANCE DEFINITIONS in Section 1, what does critical altitude mean?
options: The altitude below which engine failure is most likely
The altitude where VNE must first be reduced because of density altitude
The altitude at which full throttle produces maximum allowable power (MCP or TOP)
The altitude where hovering ceiling equals service ceiling
items.explanation: Section 1 PERFORMANCE DEFINITIONS defines critical altitude as the altitude at which full throttle produces maximum allowable power (MCP or TOP).
references: R44 II POH Sec 1: PERFORMANCE DEFINITIONS (p.1-6)
